proposed_widenings.name: teleport
proposed_widenings.justification: Dimension Door's primary mechanic is voluntary, caster-chosen positional displacement to a destination within range. This is not `transport_exile` (which is involuntary planar banishment) and is not `move` or `force_move` (which are constrained traversal). Teleportation bypasses intervening space, walls, and terrain — it is mechanically distinct from movement. No v4 atom covers voluntary same-plane short-range teleportation.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You teleport to a location within range. You arrive at exactly the spot desired.

proposed_widenings.name: teleport_phase (ActivationPhase variant)
proposed_widenings.justification: The existing `ActivationPhase` union only has `attack_roll` and `save_gate` variants, both of which resolve against a target's defense. Dimension Door's resolution is 'declare destination, arrive there' — no binary roll against a target. A new phase kind is needed for unconditional positional displacement (possibly with an occupancy-failure branch).
proposed_widenings.evidence: You teleport to a location within range. You arrive at exactly the spot desired. It can be a place you can see, one you can visualize, or one you can describe by stating distance and direction.

proposed_widenings.name: teleport_companion (Attachment or secondary-target grammar)
proposed_widenings.justification: The spell can bring one willing creature within 5 ft of the caster to a space within 5 ft of the destination. This is an optional companion-inclusion that is distinct from the `target` attachment (which models creatures the spell acts ON) and from `area` attachment. No existing attachment kind models 'bring willing creature in adjacency to caster along for the teleport'.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You can also teleport one willing creature. The creature must be within 5 feet of you when you teleport, and it teleports to a space within 5 feet of your destination space.

proposed_widenings.name: occupancy_failure_branch
proposed_widenings.justification: The damage rider 'if you or the companion would arrive in an occupied/filled space, take 4d6 Force and the teleportation fails' is not a save_gate or attack_roll. It is a positional-precondition branch: at resolution time, check destination occupancy; if blocked, apply damage and void the displacement. No existing resolution or window atom models a 'destination-occupancy check with damage-and-cancel on failure' outcome.
proposed_widenings.evidence: If you, the other creature, or both would arrive in a space occupied by a creature or completely filled by one or more objects, you and any creature traveling with you each take 4d6 Force damage, and the teleportation fails.

notes: Dimension Door's core mechanic — unconditional voluntary teleportation to a caster-chosen destination — requires a new atom (`teleport`) not in v4. The existing `transport_exile` atom is a close surface cousin but models involuntary planar exile, not voluntary in-plane short-range teleportation. The `activation` family is the correct family, but the `ActivationPhase` type needs a new variant for 'teleport to destination' since neither `attack_roll` nor `save_gate` describes this resolution. The occupancy-failure damage branch is a secondary widening: it is not a save_gate (no target makes a save) and not an attack_roll, but a positional constraint that applies damage and cancels the effect when the destination is blocked.
